title: Shard-granular SLI ingest, failover diagnosis canvases, and adaptive shed telemetry
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a shard-aware SLI ingestion pipeline and corresponding dashboard canvases that make multi-region failover and load-shedding root-cause diagnosable at token granularity without destabilizing serving performance. This ticket scopes metrics collection, sampling strategy, backend rollups, dashboard surfaces, alert wiring, and a staged rollout plan with canary probes. The outcome should let oncall and SREs quickly determine whether a degradation was caused by admission throttling, KV cache misses, decode tail latency, or cross-region fanout congestion.
context_and_background: We currently emit per-request golden signals and a sampled set of token timing traces, but it's hard to map a spike in p99 token latency to a shard or admission policy. Recent incidents (see ENG-48888 and ENG-24691) highlighted ambiguous failover behavior during cross-region spillback. This work stitches together finer-grained ingest from edge shards, a low-cost synthetic probe for shard health, and dashboard panels that correlate admit-score, kv-hit, and decode-time distributions across tenants and regions.
acceptance_criteria: A shard-level SLI ingest pipeline that accepts token-level timing tags with configurable sampling (default 1-in-500) and enriches with shard_id, region, model_variant, and route_id
Retention and rollups: raw sampled token traces stored for 7 days; tiled rollups (1m/5m) for 30 days; aggregated histograms for 90 days
Dashboard: a set of canvases showing per-shard token p50/p95/p99, admit-score distribution, kv-hit ratio, decode-time waterfall, and recent circuit-breaker events correlated on a timeline
Alerting: SLI-based alerts for shard p99 regression (relative and absolute) with playbook links; automated suppression if canary probes indicate non-production load
End-to-end test: synthetic shard probe that can induce a known pattern (kv miss storm) and the dashboard correctly surfaces the signal within 60s
No more than 2.5% additional CPU or 1% additional p95 latency on the serving path when probe/sampling enabled at default rates (measure via canary)
Runbook: documented triage steps and escalation paths in Confluence linked from the dashboard

Implement sampling sidecar to batch+compress token timing and emit to metrics pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/1122)
Schema: add shard_id and admit_score to token-sli proto and update ingestion lambda
Rollups: build streaming job to compute histogram rollups and kv-hit ratios per shard-region (stream job branch: telemetry/shard-rollup)
Dashboard: create canvases in Console: 'Shard SLI Explorer', 'Failover Diagnosis Timeline', 'Admission vs Decode Correlator'

decisions_and_tradeoffs: Sampling rate: chosen default 1-in-500 to balance observability with CPU/egress cost; canary tests required to validate upper bound for high-traffic tenants
Payload design: use compact binary proto for token timing to reduce egress; this trades readability for reduced cost and required step to update ingestion lambda to decode protos
Aggregation cadence: 1m rollups chosen to keep dashboard latency low; longer rollups (5m) used for 30-day views to reduce storage
Probe approach: synthetic probe runs as a separate tenant to avoid impacting production tenants; probe uses small batch sizes to emulate golden-signal stress patterns
Circuit-breaker correlation: we'll ingest circuit state change events into the timeline but not rely on them as triggers for automated rollbacks in this phase
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: high-cardinality shard metrics could overwhelm the metrics backend. Mitigation: limit shard cardinality by coalescing low-traffic shards to 'shard-bucket-*' and allow dynamic pruning
Risk: sampling bias hides tail issues for small tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant override for sampling and targeted synthetic probes during investigations
Risk: rollout could increase p95 latency. Mitigation: staged canary with performance gates (automated rollback if p95 regresses > 3%)
